title: Inference deep-dive sprint notes — Omar Hassan (Nov 2026)
content:
Sprint context and quick purpose:
- Two-week focused sprint: understand recent KV-cache work, quantify tradeoffs for latency vs memory, and prototype an eviction policy experiment.
- Goal: actionable knobs we can surface in Redwood Console (approx: 2–3 UI controls + sane defaults).

High-level takeaways (top-of-mind):
- Paper: "Sparse KV Caching for Long-Context Models" (arXiv 2409.x): key idea is chunk-level skip lists rather than token-level cache. Big wins for memory when contexts have repetitive blocks (e.g., code repositories, logs).
  - Practical implication: our current per-token KV cache is accurate but wasteful on repeated long prefixes. Consider a chunking abstraction at runtime (64-token or 256-token chunk sizes) and a fast bloom filter to check hits.
- Quantization experiments (4-bit vs 8-bit): signficant memory reduction at minimal per-token latency increase on A100 and GH200; but tail latency spikes if dequantize-per-step (avoid dequantize in main loop).
- Batching: continuous-batching gains are workload dependent; for interactive traces with small bursts, small window async batching (20–40ms) gives best p99 tradeoff. For steady throughput, larger windows + dynamic batch shaping wins.

Notes from reading / quick summaries:
- "Chunked KV caching" idea:
  - Pros: reduces KV footprint for repeated prefixes; cache eviction simpler; less KV shuffling across GPUs.
  - Cons: requires mapping predicted token indices to chunk ids (edge cases on subword boundary), can increase cache miss ratio for high-entropy text.
  - Implementation sketch: keep map chunk_id -> compressed KV blob. On request: check bloom filter, if hit fetch and decompress; else fallback to normal attention recompute for that chunk.

- "Quantized kernel scheduling" (ops-level scheduling paper):
  - Kernel-level scheduling that prefers int4/8 kernels when sequence length is < threshold, float16 for long seqs.
  - We should add a scheduling policy that is model-aware and length-aware: pick kernel by (model_shard_size, seq_len, latency_target).

Experiment log (local labbox tests)
- Setup: gh200x2, test model: open-llm-clone/llama-asia-7b (fp16 baseline), sequences sampled from prod-sim-logs (customer anonymized).
- Cache chunking experiment (chunk=128):
  - mem_before: ~12.2GB per GPU; mem_after_chunked: ~8.0GB (approx 34% reduction)
  - throughput change: -6% tokens/s (due to chunk decompress overhead)
  - p99 latency: +12–18ms on interactive queries (bad) but recoverable with async prefetching.
  - takeaway: chunked cache is promising for memory-bound configs (dedicated pools with lower memory) and less desirable in latency-SLO tight hosted endpoints unless prefetching present.

- Quantization microbench: int4 static per-weight quantization, dequantize-on-load vs kernel-native int4:
  - dequantize-on-load: lower CPU overhead but big memory spike during load, occasional GC stutter.
  - kernel-native int4: steady-state lower memory, slightly higher single-token latency but stable p99.
  - recommended: offer kernel-native int4 as opt-in for dedicated customers; hosted: default to int8 where available.

Code snippets / pseudo-commands I ran:
- run small experiment locally:
  - python tools/run_infer.py --model llama-asia-7b --cache-chunk=128 --async-prefetch --seq=1024 --batch=1
- profiling collection: perf record + nvprof to compare memcpy patterns

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
1) Eviction policy that is chunk-aware: LRU at chunk granularity might be suboptimal for mixed workloads. Consider LFU with age decay. Quick sim: run synthetic generator with 70% repeated prefix, 30% novel.
2) Prefetch heuristics: simple rule: if request length > chunk_size * 2 prefetch next N chunks; but aggressive prefetch costs memory. Need a cost model.
3) Integration with router and fallback policies: chunked cache may be incompatible with some fallback model variants—ensure versions agree on chunking semantics.
4) UX knobs for Console: propose three toggles: cache_mode (token|chunk), quant_mode (fp16|int8|int4), prefetch (off|auto|aggressive). Need sane defaults and guardrails for hosted.

Meeting notes with Li & Priya (2026-11-06)
- Li: wants chunking for on-prem customers who frequently upload large code corpora. Concern: chunk boundaries may split semantically-important tokens (strings, identifiers). Suggest: make chunking boundary align to sentence or newline heuristics when possible.
- Priya: quantization rollout plan: start with experiments in Dedicated pools only, add monitoring for hallucination/regression (run eval set A/B). Also wants a staged feature flag pipeline.

Mini-eval plan (for next sprint)
- Build small eval harness: 500 prompts across documents, code, chat transcripts. Measure: perplexity drift, rouge/bleu where applicable, output token distribution changes, and a small human-in-the-loop quality check.
- Monitor: cost per 1k tokens, GPU memory footprint, p50/p95/p99 latency.

Notes-to-self (practical reminders)
- When testing int4, run multiple model seeds; quant noise interacts oddly with beam search and sampling temperature.
- Use synthetic long-replay traces to stress eviction policy quickly (
  - generator: 80% repeated prefix, 10% short novel queries, 10% long novel sequences).

References and follow-ups I want to read more carefully:
- Sparse attention + KV compression work from NeurIPS 2025 (paper + appendix has useful pseudo-code).
- Runtime PR #842 on GitHub for the new chunked-cache prototype (heavily commented, needs perf tweaks).

Immediate next steps (Nov 8–14):
- Implement simple LFU-with-decay sim and run synthetic workload (owner: Omar).
- Add a console feature spec draft for toggles above and get Priya review (owner: Omar + Priya).
- Schedule 30m sync with infra team to validate memory accounting on gh200x2 (owner: Li).

Random scribbles / heuristics that might be useful later:
- If repeated-prefix-mass > 40% then chunk_size=256 gives best mem/latency ratio in our sim.
- Prefetch budget should be a soft limit expressed as fraction of total KV memory (e.g., 0.15 = only prefetch if estimated extra mem < 15% of KV pool).

End of sprint notes. Keep this as working doc — will turn into a short RFC if experiments look promising.

— Omar
